title.zh: 卷一百七十二 列傳第九十七 于王二杜范
title.en: Volume 172 Biographies 97: Yu, Wang, Two Du's, Fan
title.raw: 卷一百七十二 列傳第九十七 于王二杜范 Volume 172 Biographies 97: Yu, Wang, Two Du's, Fan

sentences.zh: 于王二杜範

translations.literal: Yu, Wang, the two Du's, and Fan
translations.idiomatic: Yu, Wang, the two members of the Du clan, and Fan

sentences.zh: 于頔，字允元，後周太師謹七世孫。

translations.literal: Yu Di, courtesy name Yunyuan, was the seventh-generation descendant of Jin, Grand Tutor of Later Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Di, style name Yunyuan, was a seventh-generation descendant of Yu Jin, grand tutor of Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 蔭補千牛，調華陰尉，累勞遷侍御史。

translations.literal: Through yin privilege he was appointed to the Thousand-Ox [Guard], was transferred to be magistrate of Huayin, and through accumulated merit was promoted to attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service by hereditary privilege as a Thousand-Ox guardsman, served as magistrate of Huayin, and rose by successive merit to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 為吐蕃計會使，有專對材。

translations.literal: He served as commissioner for Tibetan accounts and had talent for exclusive replies.
translations.idiomatic: As envoy for Tibetan fiscal matters, he proved adept at handling diplomatic exchanges on his own.

sentences.zh: 擢長安令、駕部郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to magistrate of Chang'an and director in the Department of the Imperial Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to magistrate of Chang'an and then director in the Bureau of the Imperial Carriage.

sentences.zh: 出為湖州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as prefect of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 部有湖陂，異時溉田三千頃，久廞廢，頔行縣，命脩復堤閼，歲獲粳稻蒲魚無慮萬計。

translations.literal: Within his prefecture was a lake embankment that once irrigated three thousand qing of fields; it had long been silted up and abandoned. Di toured the counties, ordered the dikes and sluices restored, and annually obtained no less than tens of thousands [of units] in japonica rice, cattails, and fish.
translations.idiomatic: His district held a lake dam that had once watered three thousand qing of farmland but had long fallen idle. On circuit through the counties, Di ordered the dikes and floodgates repaired; each year the yield in rice, reeds, and fish ran to tens of thousands of units.

sentences.zh: 州地庳薄，葬者不掩柩，頔為坎，瘞枯骨千餘，人賴以安。

translations.literal: The prefectural land was low and poor; those who buried did not cover their coffins. Di dug pits and buried more than a thousand dried bones, and the people relied on this for peace.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was low-lying and impoverished, and people often buried the dead without covering the coffins. Di had pits dug and interred more than a thousand exposed bones, to the people's great relief.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改蘇州。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was reassigned to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 罷淫祠，浚溝澮，端路衢，為政有績。

translations.literal: He abolished illicit shrines, dredged canals and ditches, and straightened roads and thoroughfares; his administration achieved results.
translations.idiomatic: He shut down unauthorized shrines, dredged canals, and put the roads in order, and his governance won a solid record.

sentences.zh: 然暴橫少恩，杖前部尉以逞憾，觀察使王緯以聞，德宗不省。

translations.literal: Yet he was violent and overbearing and short on kindness; he beat a former subordinate commandant to vent a grudge. Observation commissioner Wang Wei reported this, but Emperor Dezong took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was brutal and unforgiving: he had a former subordinate commandant flogged to settle a personal score. Observation commissioner Wang Wei reported it, but Emperor Dezong paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 俄遷大理卿，為陜虢觀察使，慢言謝緯曰：「始足下劾我，三進官矣！」

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review and made observation commissioner of Shan-Guo; with a contemptuous remark he thanked Wei, saying, "At first you impeached me—and I have been promoted three ranks!"
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review and observation commissioner of Shan-Guo. He taunted Wei: "When you first impeached me, I had only just begun—and look, I've been promoted three times since!"

sentences.zh: 益自肆。

translations.literal: He became all the more unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: He grew even more brazen.

sentences.zh: 峻罰苛懲，官吏惴恐，皆重足一跡。

translations.literal: His punishments were severe and his penalties harsh; officials were fearful and anxious, all walking as if on overlapping feet with only one footprint.
translations.idiomatic: He imposed harsh fines and cruel punishments until officials lived in dread and scarcely dared move.

sentences.zh: 參軍事姚峴不勝虐，自沈於河。

translations.literal: Staff adviser Yao Xian could not endure the cruelty and drowned himself in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Staff adviser Yao Xian, unable to bear the abuse, threw himself into the river.

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年，拜山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan he was appointed military governor of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan year 14 he was made military governor of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 是時，吳少誠叛，頔率兵自唐州戰吳房朗山，取之，禽其將李璨，又勝之濯神溝。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Shaocheng rebelled; Di led troops from Tangzhou to fight at Langshan in Wufang, took it, captured his general Li Can, and again defeated him at the Zhoushen Ravine.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Shaocheng rebelled, Di led troops from Tangzhou, fought at Langshan in Wufang, captured the place, took his general Li Can prisoner, and won again at Zhoushen Ravine.

sentences.zh: 於是請升襄州為大都督府，廣募戰士，儲良械，撊然有專漢南意，所牾者類治以軍法。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested that Xiangzhou be elevated to a great metropolitan prefecture, broadly recruited warriors, and stored fine weapons; he clearly harbored the intention of dominating the south of the Han, and those who opposed him were generally dealt with under military law.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked that Xiangzhou be raised to a metropolitan prefecture, recruited soldiers widely, and stockpiled arms; he plainly aimed to dominate the region south of the Han, and he routinely punished dissent with military law.

sentences.zh: 帝晚務姑息，頔所奏建，無不開允。

translations.literal: The emperor in his later years pursued indulgence and forbearance; whatever Di memorialized and proposed was invariably approved.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor favored appeasement, and every proposal Di submitted won approval.

sentences.zh: 公斂私輸，持下益急，而慢於奉上。

translations.literal: He collected publicly and delivered privately; he grew ever harsher toward subordinates while showing disrespect toward the court above.
translations.idiomatic: He levied taxes in public and kept the proceeds for himself, tightened his grip on subordinates, and treated the throne with contempt.

sentences.zh: 誣劾鄧州刺史元洪，朝廷重違，為流端州，命中人護送至棗陽。

translations.literal: He falsely impeached Yuan Hong, prefect of Dengzhou; the court, loath to refuse, exiled Hong to Duanzhou and ordered a eunuch to escort him as far as Zaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He framed Dengzhou prefect Yuan Hong; reluctant to defy him, the court exiled Hong to Duanzhou and sent a eunuch to escort him to Zaoyang.

sentences.zh: 頔遣兵劫洪還，拘之，表責洪太重，改吉州長史，遣使厚諭乃已。

translations.literal: Di sent troops to seize Hong on the road and bring him back, detained him, and memorialized that Hong's punishment was too severe; he was changed to chief administrator of Jizhou, and only after Di sent envoys with lavish persuasion did the matter end.
translations.idiomatic: Di sent soldiers to intercept Hong and bring him back, held him captive, and memorialized that Hong's sentence was excessive; Hong was reassigned as chief administrator of Jizhou, and Di sent envoys with rich gifts before he would let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 嘗怒判官薛正倫，奏貶陜州長史，比詔下，頔中悔，奏復署舊職。

translations.literal: Once, enraged at his aide Xue Zhenglun, he memorialized to demote him to chief administrator of Shanzhou; when the edict was about to issue, Di regretted it midway and memorialized to restore him to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Once, angry at his aide Xue Zhenglun, he had him demoted to chief administrator of Shanzhou; but before the edict arrived Di changed his mind and had him restored to his old post.

sentences.zh: 正倫死，以兵圍其居，強使孽子與婚。

translations.literal: When Zhenglun died, Di surrounded his residence with troops and forced his illegitimate son into marriage [with Di's family].
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenglun died, Di surrounded his house with soldiers and compelled his bastard son into a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 昵吏高洪，縱使剝下，別將陳儀不勝忿，刺殺洪，一府驚潰。

translations.literal: He favored his clerk Gao Hong and allowed him to strip subordinates; deputy general Chen Yi, unable to bear his rage, stabbed Hong to death, and the whole prefectural staff was thrown into panic and flight.
translations.idiomatic: He favored clerk Gao Hong and let him extort his subordinates; deputy general Chen Yi, enraged beyond endurance, stabbed Hong dead, throwing the whole prefectural staff into panic.

sentences.zh: 累遷檢校尚書左僕射、同中書門下平章事，封燕國公。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Grand Councilor, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Councilor, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 俄擅以兵取鄧州，天子未始誰何。

translations.literal: Soon he on his own authority took Dengzhou by force, and the Son of Heaven never once held him to account.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he seized Dengzhou by force on his own authority, and the emperor never called him to account.

sentences.zh: 初，襄有髹器，天下以為法。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiang [prefecture] had lacquerware that the realm took as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier times Xiangzhou's lacquerware set the standard for the empire.

sentences.zh: 至頔驕蹇，故方帥不法者號「襄樣節度」。

translations.literal: When Di became arrogant and obstinate, regional commanders who acted unlawfully were called "Xiang-style governors."
translations.idiomatic: When Di grew arrogant and defiant, lawless regional commanders were nicknamed "governors in the Xiang mold."

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，權綱自出，頔稍懼，願以子尚主，帝許之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne and authority issued from him alone, Di grew somewhat afraid and wished to marry his son to a princess; the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong came to the throne and power flowed from the center again, Di grew uneasy and offered his son in marriage to a princess; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂入朝，拜司空、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he entered court and was appointed Minister of Works and concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He then came to court and was appointed Minister of Works and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 請準杜佑，月三奉朝，詔可。

translations.literal: He requested to follow Du You's precedent of attending court three times a month; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to follow Du You's precedent of attending court three times a month, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 時宦者梁守謙幸於帝，頗用事。

translations.literal: At the time the eunuch Liang Shouqian was favored by the emperor and wielded considerable power.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Liang Shouqian enjoyed the emperor's favor and wielded real power at court.

sentences.zh: 有梁正言者，與頔子敏善，敏因正言厚賂守謙，求頔出鎮。

translations.literal: There was one Liang Zhengyan, friendly with Di's son Min; through Zhengyan, Min lavishly bribed Shouqian, seeking to have Di sent out to a frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zhengyan was close to Di's son Min, and Min used him to bribe Shouqian heavily, hoping to get his father posted back to a military command.

sentences.zh: 久不報，敏怒其紿，責所饋，誘正言家奴支解之，棄混中。

translations.literal: When no reply came for a long time, Min grew angry at being deceived, demanded back what he had given, and induced Zhengyan's household slave to dismember him and cast the remains into a privy.
translations.idiomatic: When nothing came of it for a long time, Min decided he had been cheated, demanded his gifts back, and had Zhengyan's slave dismember him and dump the body in a privy.

sentences.zh: 家童上變，詔捕頔吏沈壁及它奴送御史獄，命中丞薛存誠、刑部侍郎王播、大理卿武少儀雜問之。

translations.literal: A household boy reported the crime; an edict ordered the arrest of Di's clerk Shen Bi and the other slaves and their delivery to the censorate prison, and commanded Vice Censor-in-Chief Xue Cuncheng, Vice Minister of Justice Wang Bo, and Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Wu Shaoyi jointly to interrogate them.
translations.idiomatic: A household servant reported the crime; the court ordered Di's clerk Shen Bi and the other slaves arrested and sent to the censorate prison, with Vice Censor-in-Chief Xue Cuncheng, Vice Minister of Justice Wang Bo, and Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Wu Shaoyi assigned to conduct a joint inquiry.

sentences.zh: 頔與諸子素服待罪建福門，門史不內，屏營負墻立，更遣人上章，有司拒不聞。

translations.literal: Di and his sons, in plain dress awaiting punishment, waited at the Jianfu Gate; the gate clerk would not admit them. They stood in trepidation with their backs to the wall, again sent someone to submit a memorial, and the responsible offices refused to hear it.
translations.idiomatic: Di and his sons waited in plain dress to accept punishment at the Jianfu Gate, but the gatekeeper would not let them in. They stood trembling against the wall, sent another memorial, and the authorities refused to receive it.

sentences.zh: 翌日復往，宰相諭使還第。

translations.literal: The next day they went again; the chief ministers instructed them to return to their residence.
translations.idiomatic: They returned the next day, but the chief ministers told them to go home.

sentences.zh: 貶為恩王傅，子敏竄雷州，至商山，賜死。

translations.literal: Di was demoted to tutor of the Prince of En; his son Min was banished to Leizhou, and at Shangshan he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Di was demoted to tutor of the Prince of En; his son Min was exiled to Leizhou and, at Shangshan, ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 次子季友奪二官，正及方免官。

translations.literal: His second son Jiyou was stripped of two ranks; Zheng and Fang were dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Jiyou lost two ranks; Zheng and Fang were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 流壁封州，正言誅死。

translations.literal: Bi was exiled to Fengzhou; Zhengyan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was exiled to Fengzhou; Zhengyan was put to death.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝討蔡，頔獻家財以助國，帝卻之。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned against Cai, Di offered his family wealth to aid the state; the emperor declined it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against Cai, Di offered his family fortune to support the war effort, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 又坐季友居喪荒宴，削金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Again, because Jiyou during mourning held dissolute feasts, Di was stripped of his Golden Purple Radiance Grand Master title.
translations.idiomatic: He was also stripped of his Golden Purple Radiance Grand Master rank because Jiyou held riotous feasts while in mourning.

sentences.zh: 帝初欲頔告老，宰相李逢吉謂得謝乃優禮，非所以示責。

translations.literal: The emperor at first wished Di to request retirement; Chief Minister Li Fengji said that granting leave would be a mark of favor, not a way to show censure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor first wanted Di to retire, but Chief Minister Li Fengji argued that granting retirement would look like an honor, not a punishment.

sentences.zh: 明年，乃致仕。

translations.literal: The following year he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 宰司將以太子少保官之，帝改署賓客。

translations.literal: The chief ministers were about to appoint him Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent; the emperor changed the appointment to Retainer.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers planned to make him Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, but the emperor reassigned him as Retainer instead.

sentences.zh: 郁郁不得意卒，贈太保，太常謚曰厲。

translations.literal: Dispirited and dissatisfied, he died; he was posthumously given Grand Mentor, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices gave the posthumous title Ferocious.
translations.idiomatic: He died disheartened and embittered; posthumously he was made Grand Mentor, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices gave him the posthumous name Ferocious.

sentences.zh: 頔嘗制《順聖樂舞》獻諸朝。

translations.literal: Di once composed the "Shunsheng Music and Dance" and presented it to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Di once composed the Shunsheng Music and Dance and presented it at court.

sentences.zh: 又教女伎為八佾，聲態雄侈，號《孫吳順聖樂》雲。

translations.literal: He also trained female performers in the eight-row dance; the sound and bearing were grand and extravagant, and it was called the "Sun-Wu Shunsheng Music."
translations.idiomatic: He also trained female performers in the eight-row dance; its sound and spectacle were lavish, and it was called the Sun-Wu Shunsheng Music.

sentences.zh: 季友尚憲宗永昌公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Jiyou married Emperor Xianzong's Princess Yongchang and was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Sons-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyou married Xianzong's Princess Yongchang and was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Sons-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 從穆宗獵苑中，求改頔謚，會徐泗節度使李亦為請，更賜謚曰思。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Muzong on a hunt in the park, he requested that Di's posthumous title be changed; at the same time Xu-Si military governor Li also petitioned, and a new posthumous title Reflective was granted.
translations.idiomatic: While hunting with Muzong in the imperial park, he asked that Di's posthumous name be changed; Xu-Si military governor Li petitioned as well, and the posthumous name was changed to Reflective.

sentences.zh: 尚書右丞張正甫封還詔書，右補闕高釴、博士王彥威持不可，謂：「頔文吏，倔強犯命，擅軍襄、鄧，欲脅制朝廷；

translations.literal: Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Zhang Zhengfu sealed and returned the edict; Right Remonstrance Official Gao Yu and Erudite Wang Yanwei held that it could not be done, saying, "Di was a civil official who defiantly violated orders, on his own authority garrisoned Xiang and Deng, and sought to coerce the court;
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Zhang Zhengfu sealed the edict and sent it back; Right Remonstrance Official Gao Yu and Erudite Wang Yanwei objected, saying, "Di was a civil official who defied the throne, garrisoned Xiang and Deng on his own authority, and tried to intimidate the court;

sentences.zh: 殺不辜，留制囚，遮使者，僭正樂。

translations.literal: he killed the innocent, detained prisoners under imperial decree, obstructed envoys, and usurped orthodox music.
translations.idiomatic: he killed the innocent, held prisoners against imperial orders, blocked court envoys, and arrogated court ritual music.

sentences.zh: 勢迫而朝，非其宿心，得全腰領而歿，猶以為幸，不宜更謚。」

translations.literal: Forced by circumstances he came to court—that was not his original intent; that he died with his head intact was already counted fortunate. His posthumous title should not be changed."
translations.idiomatic: He came to court only because he was cornered, not from loyalty; that he died with his head still on his shoulders was already more than he deserved. His posthumous name should not be changed."

sentences.zh: 帝不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 方，長慶時以勛家子通豪俠，欲事河朔，以策幹宰相元稹。

translations.literal: Fang, during the Changqing era, as the son of a meritorious family associated with bold knights-errant, wished to serve in Hebei and presented his stratagem to Chief Minister Yuan Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: During Changqing, Fang, scion of a meritorious house and friend to men of daring, sought a career in Hebei and brought his plans to Chief Minister Yuan Zhen.

sentences.zh: 而李逢吉黨謀傾執政，乃告稹結客刺裴度，事下有司，驗無狀，方坐誅。

translations.literal: But Li Fengji's faction plotted to topple the chief minister and reported that Zhen had retained clients to assassinate Pei Du; the matter was referred to the authorities, investigation found no substance, yet Fang was executed on the charge.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji's faction, plotting to oust the chief minister, accused Zhen of hiring assassins to kill Pei Du; though the inquiry found no proof, Fang was executed anyway.

sentences.zh: 王智興，字匡諫，懷州溫人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhixing, courtesy name Kuangjian, was a native of Wen in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhixing, style name Kuangjian, was from Wen in Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 少驍銳，為徐州牙兵，事刺史李洧。

translations.literal: In youth he was fierce and sharp; he became a yabing of Xuzhou and served Prefect Li Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was bold and keen; he served as a yabing in Xuzhou under Prefect Li Wei.

sentences.zh: 洧棄李納，挈州自歸。

translations.literal: Wei abandoned Li Na and brought the prefecture over to submit on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Wei broke with Li Na and brought the prefecture back to Tang allegiance.

sentences.zh: 納怒，急攻洧。

translations.literal: Na was enraged and pressed the attack on Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Na pressed the attack on Wei.

sentences.zh: 智興能駛步，奉表，不數日至京師告急，德宗出朔方軍五千擊納，解去，自是為徐特將。

translations.literal: Zhixing could run swiftly; he bore a memorial and in only a few days reached the capital to report the emergency. Dezong sent out five thousand Shuofang troops to strike Na, and the siege was lifted; from then on he was a special general of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixing could run at great speed; he carried a memorial and reached the capital within days to report the crisis. Dezong dispatched five thousand Shuofang troops against Na and lifted the siege; from then on Zhixing was a special general of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 討吳元濟也。

translations.literal: He also campaigned against Wu Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: He also fought in the campaign against Wu Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 李師道謀撓王師，數侵徐救蔡。

translations.literal: Li Shidao plotted to disrupt the imperial army and repeatedly invaded Xuzhou to relieve Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao tried to disrupt the imperial campaign and repeatedly raided Xuzhou to relieve Cai.

sentences.zh: 節度使李願遣智興率步騎拒賊。

translations.literal: Military governor Li Yuan sent Zhixing to lead infantry and cavalry to repel the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Military governor Li Yuan sent Zhixing with infantry and cavalry to hold the rebels off.

sentences.zh: 其將王朝晏方攻沛，智興逆擊，敗之，朝晏脫身保沂州。

translations.literal: His general Wang Chaoyan was then attacking Pei; Zhixing met him in counterattack, defeated him, and Chaoyan escaped with his life to hold Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His general Wang Chaoyan was besieging Pei when Zhixing counterattacked and routed him; Chaoyan escaped and held Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 進破姚海兵五萬於豐北，獲美妾三人，智興曰：「軍中有女子，安得不敗？」

translations.literal: Advancing, he defeated Yao Hai's fifty thousand troops north of Feng, captured three beautiful concubines, and Zhixing said, "When there are women in the army, how can one not be defeated?"
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and defeated Yao Hai's fifty thousand men north of Feng, capturing three beautiful concubines. Zhixing said, "With women in the camp, how can an army fail to lose?"

sentences.zh: 即斬以徇。

translations.literal: He immediately beheaded them as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: He had them beheaded at once as an example.

sentences.zh: 朝晏自沂以輕兵襲沛，夜戰狄丘，復破之。

translations.literal: Chaoyan from Yi led light troops to raid Pei; fighting by night at Diqiu, Zhixing again defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyan led light troops from Yi to raid Pei; Zhixing fought him by night at Diqiu and routed him again.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍御史。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 元和十三年，伐師道，智興以步騎八千次胡陵，與忠武軍會，以騎畀其子晏平、晏宰為先鋒，自率軍繼之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe, campaigning against Shidao, Zhixing with eight thousand infantry and cavalry encamped at Huling, joined the Zhongwu army, gave the cavalry to his sons Yanping and Yanzai as vanguard, and himself led the army in support.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe year 13, campaigning against Shidao, Zhixing encamped eight thousand infantry and cavalry at Huling, joined the Zhongwu army, put his sons Yanping and Yanzai at the head of the cavalry vanguard, and followed with the main force.

sentences.zh: 壞河橋，收黃隊，攻金鄉，拔魚臺，俘斬萬計。

translations.literal: He destroyed the river bridge, took Huangdui, attacked Jinxiang, captured Yutai, and captured or killed no less than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed the river bridge, took Huangdui, attacked Jinxiang, captured Yutai, and killed or captured tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 賊平，進御史中丞。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was promoted to censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were subdued, he was promoted to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 明年，召還，為沂州刺史。

translations.literal: The following year he was recalled and made prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was recalled and appointed prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，河朔用兵，加檢校左散騎常侍，充武寧軍副使、河北行營諸軍都知兵馬使，帥兵三千度河。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing, when troops were deployed in Hebei, he was given the additional title of acting Left Regular Attendant, made deputy commissioner of the Wuning army and overall commander of troops and horses for the Hebei field headquarters, and led three thousand men across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Changqing, when war broke out in Hebei, he was made acting Left Regular Attendant, deputy commissioner of the Wuning army, and overall commander of the Hebei field forces, and led three thousand men across the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 屬朝廷用崔群為武寧節度使，群畏智興難制，密請追還京師，未報。

translations.literal: Just then the court appointed Cui Qun military governor of Wuning; Qun feared Zhixing would be hard to control and secretly requested that he be recalled to the capital; no reply had come.
translations.idiomatic: The court had just appointed Cui Qun military governor of Wuning; fearing Zhixing would be hard to control, Qun secretly asked that he be recalled to the capital, but no answer had yet come.

sentences.zh: 會赦王廷湊，諸節度班師。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Tingcou was pardoned, and the various military governors withdrew their armies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingcou was pardoned, and the regional armies withdrew.

sentences.zh: 智興還，群遣寮屬迎之，令士季甲而入。

translations.literal: When Zhixing returned, Qun sent staff members to welcome him and ordered the soldiers to enter in armor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixing returned, Qun sent staff to welcome him and ordered the troops to enter in full armor.

sentences.zh: 智興心不悅，因勒兵斬關入，殺異己者十餘輩，然後謁群謝曰：「此軍情也！」

translations.literal: Zhixing was displeased at heart; he thereupon marshaled troops, cut through the pass, and entered, killing more than ten who differed from him, then went to see Qun and apologized, saying, "This was the army's sentiment!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhixing took offense, rallied his troops, forced the gate, and killed more than ten rivals before calling on Qun to apologize: "That was the army's doing!"

sentences.zh: 群乃治裝去，智興以兵衛送還朝；

translations.literal: Qun then packed to leave; Zhixing escorted him back to court with troops;
translations.idiomatic: Qun packed to leave; Zhixing escorted him back to the capital under armed guard;

sentences.zh: 至埇橋，掠鹽鐵院及貢物，劫商旅，逐濠州刺史侯弘度。

translations.literal: at Yongqiao he plundered the Salt and Iron Commission depot and tribute goods, robbed merchants and travelers, and drove out Hao prefect Hou Hongdu.
translations.idiomatic: at Yongqiao he looted the Salt and Iron Commission depot and tribute goods, robbed merchants, and expelled Hao prefect Hou Hongdu.

sentences.zh: 朝廷甫罷兵，不能討，即詔檢校工部尚書，充本軍節度使。

translations.literal: The court had just demobilized and could not punish him; it immediately issued an edict making him acting Minister of Works and commissioner of his own army.
translations.idiomatic: The court had just stood down its armies and could not move against him; it promptly appointed him acting Minister of Works and military governor of his own command.

sentences.zh: 智興由是揫索財賂，交權幸以賈虛名，用度不足，始稅泗口以佐軍須。

translations.literal: Zhixing thereupon extorted wealth and goods, cultivated favorites to purchase empty reputation, and when expenses were insufficient began taxing Sikou to supplement military needs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixing then extorted wealth, curried favor with powerful courtiers to buy prestige, and when funds ran short began levying taxes at Sikou to pay for his army.

sentences.zh: 李攻宋州，智興悉銳師出宋西鄙，破之漳口。

translations.literal: When Li attacked Songzhou, Zhixing led all his crack troops out to Song's western border and defeated him at Zhangkou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li attacked Songzhou, Zhixing marched all his best troops to Song's western frontier and defeated him at Zhangkou.

sentences.zh: 平，加檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: When the rebellion was pacified, he was given the additional title of acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, he was made acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 李同捷以滄德叛，智興請悉師三萬賫五月糧討賊，詔拜檢校司徒、同中書門下平章事、滄德行營招撫使。

translations.literal: When Li Tongjie rebelled in Cang-De, Zhixing requested to lead all his troops, thirty thousand, with five months' provisions to campaign against the rebels; an edict appointed him acting Minister of Education, concurrent Grand Councilor, and pacification commissioner of the Cang-De field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Tongjie rebelled in Cang-De, Zhixing asked to lead his full force of thirty thousand with five months' rations; the court appointed him acting Minister of Education, Grand Councilor, and pacification commissioner for the Cang-De campaign.

sentences.zh: 既戰，降其將十輩、銳士三千，遂拔棣州。

translations.literal: After fighting, he induced the surrender of ten of their generals and three thousand crack troops, and then captured Dizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he won over ten enemy generals and three thousand elite troops, then took Dizhou.

sentences.zh: 諸將聞，戰愈力，遂有功。

translations.literal: When the other generals heard of this, they fought all the harder and thereby achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, the other generals fought harder and won their share of glory.

sentences.zh: 入朝，燕麟德殿，賜予備厚。

translations.literal: He entered court; a banquet was held in the Linde Hall and gifts were lavish.
translations.idiomatic: He came to court, was feasted in the Linde Hall, and received lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 冊拜太傅，封雁門郡王，進兼侍中。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed by imperial patent as Grand Tutor, created Prince of Yanmen Commandery, and advanced to concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Grand Tutor, created Prince of Yanmen, and promoted to concurrent Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 改忠武、河中、宣武三節度。

translations.literal: He was transferred among the three commands of Zhongwu, Hezhong, and Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as military governor of Zhongwu, Hezhong, and Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十九，贈太尉。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-nine and was posthumously given Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-nine and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子九人，晏平、宰知名。

translations.literal: He had nine sons; Yanping and Yanzai were the best known.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine sons; Yanping and Yanzai were the most notable.

sentences.zh: 晏平幼從父軍，以討同捷功，檢校右散騎常侍、朔方靈鹽節度使。

translations.literal: Yanping from youth followed his father in the army; for merit in campaigning against Tongjie he was made acting Right Regular Attendant and military governor of Shuofang-Ling-Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanping had followed his father on campaign from boyhood; for his service against Tongjie he was made acting Right Regular Attendant and military governor of Shuofang-Ling-Yan.

sentences.zh: 父喪，擅取馬四百、兵械七千自衛歸洛陽。

translations.literal: When his father died, on his own authority he took four hundred horses and seven thousand weapons for self-protection and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On his father's death he took four hundred horses and seven thousand weapons without authorization and marched back to Luoyang under escort.

sentences.zh: 御史劾之，有詔流康州，不即行，陰求援於河北三鎮。

translations.literal: The censors impeached him; an edict exiled him to Kangzhou, but he did not depart at once and secretly sought aid from the three Hebei commands.
translations.idiomatic: The censors impeached him; he was exiled to Kangzhou but did not go, and secretly appealed to the three Hebei commands for help.

sentences.zh: 三鎮表其困，改撫州司馬。

translations.literal: The three commands memorialized on his hardship, and his sentence was changed to military adjutant of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The three commands petitioned on his behalf, and he was reassigned as military adjutant of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 給事中韋溫、薛廷老、盧弘宣等還詔不敢下，改永州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Drafting officials Wei Wen, Xue Tinglao, Lu Hongxuan, and others returned the edict and dared not issue it; he was changed to revenue clerk of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting officials Wei Wen, Xue Tinglao, and Lu Hongxuan returned the edict unissued; he was reassigned as revenue clerk of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 溫固執，文宗諭而止。

translations.literal: Wei persisted; Emperor Wenzong instructed him and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Wei held firm until Wenzong instructed him to stop.

sentences.zh: 晏宰，後去「晏」，獨名宰。

translations.literal: Yan Zai, afterward he removed "Yan" and was known by the single name Zai.
translations.idiomatic: He was called Yan Zai at first, but later dropped the generational name "Yan" and went by Zai alone.

sentences.zh: 少拳果，長隸神策軍。

translations.literal: In youth he was forceful in boxing; in age he served in the Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was bold and pugilistic; as an adult he enlisted in the Shence Army.

sentences.zh: 甘露之變，以功兼御史大夫，為光州刺史。

translations.literal: At the Sweet Dew Incident, for merit he was concurrently made Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sweet Dew Incident he distinguished himself and was made Vice Censor-in-Chief while serving as prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 有美政，觀察使段文昌薦之朝，除鹽州刺史。

translations.literal: His governance was excellent; observation commissioner Duan Wenchang recommended him to the court, and he was appointed prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He governed well, and observation commissioner Duan Wenchang recommended him to the throne; he was then made prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 持法嚴，人不甚便。

translations.literal: He held the law strictly, and the people found it not very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He enforced the law with severity, and the populace did not much relish it.

sentences.zh: 累擢邠寧慶節度使。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he became military governor of Binning-Qing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to military governor of Binning-Qing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 回鶻平，徙忠武軍。

translations.literal: When the Uyghurs were pacified, he was transferred to the Zhongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: After the Uyghur campaign was settled, he was reassigned to the Zhongwu command.

sentences.zh: 討劉稹也，詔宰以兵出魏博，趨磁州。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhen was being suppressed, an edict ordered Zai to lead troops out from Weibo and advance on Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Liu Zhen, the emperor ordered Zai to march from Weibo toward Cizhou at the head of his troops.

sentences.zh: 當是時，何弘敬陰首鼠，聞宰至，大懼，即引軍濟漳水。

translations.literal: At that time He Hongjing secretly wavered like a rat; hearing Zai had arrived, he was greatly afraid and immediately led his army across the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: He Hongjing was then hedging his bets in secret; when he learned Zai was coming he panicked and at once crossed the Zhang River with his army.

sentences.zh: 宰相李德裕建言：「河陽兵寡，以忠武為援，既以捍洛，則並制魏博。」

translations.literal: Chief minister Li Deyu offered counsel: "Heyang has few troops; use Zhongwu as reinforcement—once Luoyang is shielded, Weibo can be controlled together."
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister Li Deyu argued: "Heyang's garrison is thin; Zhongwu should reinforce it—protect Luoyang and Weibo falls into our grip as well."

sentences.zh: 遂詔宰以兵五千椎鋒，兼統河陽行營。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Zai with five thousand troops as the vanguard and concurrently to command the Heyang field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accordingly put Zai at the head of five thousand shock troops and gave him overall command of the Heyang field camp.

sentences.zh: 進取天井關，賊黨離沮。

translations.literal: He advanced and took Tianjing Pass; the rebels' partisans scattered in dismay.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Tianjing Pass, and the rebel host broke apart in discouragement.

sentences.zh: 德裕以宰乘破竹勢不遂取澤州，以其子晏實守磁，為顧望計，帝有詔切責。

translations.literal: Because Zai, though pressing with irresistible momentum, did not promptly seize Zezhou—his son Yan Shi holding Cizhou as a scheme of watchful delay—the emperor issued an edict sharply rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: Zai had the momentum of a bamboo split wide open yet stalled before Zezhou while his son Yan Shi guarded Cizhou—a feint of hesitation—and the emperor sent down a stern rebuke.

sentences.zh: 宰懼，急攻陵川，破賊石會關，進攻澤州。

translations.literal: Zai was afraid; he urgently attacked Lingchuan, broke the rebel Shi Hui Pass, and advanced to attack Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened, Zai rushed to assault Lingchuan, stormed the rebel strongpoint at Shihui Pass, and pressed the attack on Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 其將郭誼殺稹降。

translations.literal: His general Guo Yi killed Zhen and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate Guo Yi killed Liu Zhen and capitulated.

sentences.zh: 宰傳稹首京師，遂節度太原。

translations.literal: Zai sent Zhen's head to the capital and was then made military governor of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zai forwarded Liu Zhen's head to the capital and was appointed military governor of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初，入朝，厚結權幸求宰相，周墀劾之，乃還軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanzong's reign he entered court, cultivated the powerful and favored to seek the chancellorship; Zhou Chi impeached him, and he then returned to his army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuanzong's reign he came to court, currying favor with the mighty to win a seat in the chancellery; Zhou Chi denounced him, and he went back to his command.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃引党項、回鶻寇河西，詔統代北諸軍進擊。

translations.literal: Tibet led Tangut and Uyghur raids on Hexi; an edict ordered him to command the armies north of Dai and advance to strike.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibet incited Tangut and Uyghur incursions into Hexi, he was ordered to take charge of the northern armies and drive them back.

sentences.zh: 以疾不任事，徙河陽。

translations.literal: Illness kept him from his duties; he was transferred to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sickness left him unable to serve, and he was reassigned to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 罷為太子少保，分司東都。

translations.literal: He was dismissed to be Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, with duties delegated at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from active command and made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, serving remotely at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 進少傅，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Junior Tutor and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Junior Tutor before his death.

sentences.zh: 晏實幼機警，智興自養之，故名與諸父齒。

translations.literal: Yan Shi was clever and alert from childhood; Zhixing raised him himself, and therefore his given name ranks with those of his paternal uncles.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi was quick-witted from boyhood; Zhixing personally reared him, so his name was placed among those of his uncles.

sentences.zh: 稹平，擢淄州刺史，終天雄節度使。

translations.literal: When Zhen was pacified he was promoted to prefect of Zizhou and ended as military governor of Tianxiong.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Zhen's defeat he was elevated to prefect of Zizhou and eventually finished his career as military governor of Tianxiong.

sentences.zh: 杜兼，字處弘，中書令正倫五世孫。

translations.literal: Du Jian, courtesy name Chuhong, was the fifth-generation descendant of Chief Minister Zhenlun.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jian, styled Chuhong, descended in the fifth generation from the Chief Minister Du Zhenlun.

sentences.zh: 初，正倫無子，故以兄子誌靜為後。

translations.literal: At first Zhenlun had no son, so he took his elder brother's son Zhijing as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenlun originally had no sons and therefore adopted his brother's son Zhijing as his heir.

sentences.zh: 父廙，為鄭州錄事參事軍事。

translations.literal: His father Yi served as registrar and adjutant in the military affairs of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi held the post of registrar and military adjutant at Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 安祿山亂，逃去，賊索之急，宋州刺史李岑以兵迎之，為追騎所害。

translations.literal: During the An Lushan rebellion he fled; the rebels sought him urgently; Songzhou prefect Li Cen came out with troops to meet him, and he was killed by pursuing horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out he fled; the rebels hunted him fiercely; Li Cen, prefect of Songzhou, marched out to receive him, but pursuing riders cut him down.

sentences.zh: 兼尚幼，逃入終南山。

translations.literal: Jian was still young and fled into Mount Zhongnan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was still a child and escaped into the Zhongnan Mountains.

sentences.zh: 伯父存介為賊執，臨刑，兼號呼願為奴以贖，遂皆免。

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Cunjie was seized by the rebels; at the moment of execution Jian cried out that he would become a slave to redeem him, and both were then spared.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels captured his uncle Cunjie and prepared to execute him, the boy Jian shouted that he would be their slave in exchange—and both lives were spared.

sentences.zh: 建中初，進士高第，徐泗節度使張建封表置其府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era he passed the presented scholar examination with high standing; Xu-Si military governor Zhang Jianfeng memorialized to place him in his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong reign he ranked high on the metropolitan examination; Zhang Jianfeng, military governor of Xu-Si, had him posted to his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 積勞為濠州刺史。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he became prefect of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After years of service he was made prefect of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 性浮險，尚豪侈。

translations.literal: By nature he was shallow and treacherous, given to lavish extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: He was frivolous and scheming by temperament, and fond of ostentatious luxury.

sentences.zh: 德宗既厭兵，大抵刺史重代易，至歷年不徙。

translations.literal: Once Emperor Dezong grew weary of warfare, for the most part prefects were frequently rotated, yet some went years without transfer.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor wearied of campaigning, prefects were usually turned over often—though some lingered in office for years on end.

sentences.zh: 兼探帝意，謀自固，即脩武備，募占勁兵三千。

translations.literal: Jian discerned the emperor's intent, plotted self-preservation, and immediately repaired defenses and recruited three thousand selected strong troops.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the throne's mood, Jian schemed to entrench himself: he fortified his defenses and raised three thousand handpicked soldiers.

sentences.zh: 帝以為才，遂橫恣。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded him as talented and he then acted with reckless license.
translations.idiomatic: The court took this as proof of his ability, and he grew ever more arbitrary and overbearing.

sentences.zh: 僚官韋賞、陸楚皆聞家子，有美譽，論事忤兼，誣劾以罪。

translations.literal: Staff officials Wei Shang and Lu Chu were both sons of renowned families with fine reputations; in discussing affairs they offended Jian, who falsely impeached them on charges.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues Wei Shang and Lu Chu—scions of distinguished houses with spotless names—crossed him in council, and he framed them on trumped-up charges.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中人至，兼廷勞畢，出詔執賞等殺之，二人無罪死，眾莫不冤。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a eunuch; after Jian had completed the audience ceremony of commendation, the edict was produced to seize Shang and the others and execute them—the two men died innocent, and none did not deem it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: A palace envoy arrived; Jian received him with full ceremony of praise, then produced an edict ordering Wei Shang and the rest seized and put to death. Innocent men were killed, and all who heard it cried injustice.

sentences.zh: 又妄系令狐運而陷李藩，欲殺之，不克。

translations.literal: He also falsely imprisoned Linghu Yun to frame Li Fan, wishing to kill him but not succeeding.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise seized Linghu Yun on false pretenses to incriminate Li Fan and tried to have him executed, but failed.

sentences.zh: 元和初，入為刑部郎中，改蘇州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era he entered court as director in the Ministry of Justice and was changed to prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he was called to the capital as a director in the Ministry of Justice, then made prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 比行，上書言李锜必反，留為吏部郎中。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, he submitted a memorial saying Li Qi would surely rebel; he was retained as director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Just before leaving for his post he memorialized that Li Qi would rebel; the throne kept him in the capital as a director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尋擢河南尹。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to metropolitan governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was elevated to metropolitan governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 杜佑素善兼，終始倚為助力。

translations.literal: Du You had long been on good terms with Jian and from first to last relied on him as a supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: Du You had always favored Jian and counted on him as a steady ally throughout.

sentences.zh: 所至大殺戮，裒蓺財貲，極耆欲。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he slaughtered on a great scale, amassed wealth, and indulged desires to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Every post he held saw bloody purges, hoarded riches, and the fullest gratification of his appetites.

sentences.zh: 適幸其時，未嘗敗。

translations.literal: He happened to be fortunate in his timing and never failed.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune smiled on his timing, and he never came to grief.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 家聚書至萬卷，署其末，以墜鬻為不孝，戒子孫雲。

translations.literal: His household gathered books to ten thousand scrolls; at the end he inscribed that to lose or sell them was unfilial, admonishing his descendants thus.
translations.idiomatic: His family library ran to ten thousand scrolls; he wrote at the end that discarding or selling them would be an act of unfilial impiety—a warning left to posterity.

sentences.zh: 從弟羔，貞元初及進士第，有至性。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Gao, at the beginning of the Zhenyuan era passed the presented scholar examination and possessed supreme filial nature.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Gao took the metropolitan degree early in the Zhenyuan reign and was distinguished by uncommon filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 父死河北，母更兵亂，不知所之，羔憂號終日。

translations.literal: His father died in Hebei; his mother was further lost in military turmoil and her whereabouts unknown; Gao grieved and wailed all day.
translations.idiomatic: His father died in Hebei; amid renewed warfare his mother vanished without trace, and Gao mourned and cried out the whole day long.

sentences.zh: 及兼為澤潞判官，鞫獄，有媼辨對不凡，乃羔母，因得奉養。

translations.literal: When Jian served as adjutant of Ze-Lu and was interrogating a case, an old woman answered with uncommon skill—it was Gao's mother, and he thus obtained her to support.
translations.idiomatic: While Jian held a judgeship on the Ze-Lu circuit and was hearing a case, an old woman's sharp replies revealed her as Gao's long-lost mother, and he was able to take her home and care for her.

sentences.zh: 而不知父墓區處，晝夜哀慟；

translations.literal: Yet he did not know the location of his father's tomb and grieved in anguish day and night;
translations.idiomatic: But he still did not know where his father's grave lay, and he wept in grief through day and night;

sentences.zh: 它日舍佛祠，觀柱間有文字，乃其父臨死記墓所在。

translations.literal: One day he lodged at a Buddhist temple and saw writing between the pillars—it was his father's dying record of where the tomb lay.
translations.idiomatic: One day he took shelter in a temple and noticed characters inscribed on a pillar—his father's last account of the burial site.

sentences.zh: 羔奔往，亦有耆老識其壟，因是得葬。

translations.literal: Gao rushed there; there were also elders who recognized the mound, and by this he was able to bury him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao hurried to the spot; village elders still knew the mound, and at last he could lay his father properly to rest.

sentences.zh: 元和中，為萬年令，時許季同為長安令，京兆尹元義方責租賦不時，系二縣吏，將罪之。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era he was magistrate of Wannian; at the time Xu Jitong was magistrate of Chang'an; metropolitan governor Yuan Yifang blamed them for untimely rent and tax collection, imprisoned the clerks of both counties, and was about to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanhe he served as magistrate of Wannian while Xu Jitong held Chang'an; the metropolitan governor Yuan Yifang faulted both counties for late tax deliveries, jailed their clerks, and prepared to punish them.

sentences.zh: 羔等辯列尤苦，尹不為縱。

translations.literal: Gao and the others argued their case with particular hardship, but the governor would not release them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao and his colleagues pleaded their case with bitter earnestness, yet the governor refused to relent.

sentences.zh: 羔乃謁宰相，請移散官。

translations.literal: Gao then visited the chief ministers and requested transfer to an honorary post.
translations.idiomatic: Gao went to the chief ministers and asked to be moved to an inactive honorary rank.

sentences.zh: 憲宗遣中使問狀，具對府政苛細，力不堪奉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong sent a palace envoy to inquire into the matter; he fully replied that the prefectural administration was harsh and meticulous and his strength could not bear service.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong dispatched an imperial messenger to investigate; Gao explained in full that the prefect's rule was petty and exacting beyond what he could endure.

sentences.zh: 詔皆免官，奪尹三月俸。

translations.literal: An edict dismissed all from office and stripped the governor of three months' salary.
translations.idiomatic: An edict removed both magistrates from office and docked the governor three months' pay.

sentences.zh: 議者以羔為直。

translations.literal: Commentators regarded Gao as upright.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion held that Gao had acted with integrity.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授戶部郎中，後歷振武節度使，以工部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed director in the Ministry of Revenue; later he served as military governor of Zhenwu and retired as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made a director in the Ministry of Revenue, later military governor of Zhenwu, and finally retired as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書右僕射，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and canonized as Jing ("Reverent").
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously honored as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, with the posthumous name Reverent.

sentences.zh: 子中立，字無為，以門蔭歷太子通事舍人。

translations.literal: His son Zhongli, courtesy name Wuwei, through yin privilege served successively as courier attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongli, styled Wuwei, entered service through family privilege as courier attendant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 開成初，文宗欲以真源、臨真二公主降士族，謂宰相曰：「民間脩婚姻，不計官品而上閥閱。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaicheng era, Emperor Wenzong wished to marry the Princesses Zhenyuan and Linzhen to gentry families and said to the chief ministers: "Among the people in arranging marriages, they do not consider official rank but esteem clan pedigree.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaicheng, Wenzong meant to marry the Princesses Zhenyuan and Linzhen into great clans and told his chief ministers: "Common folk arranging marriages care nothing for office and everything for pedigree.

sentences.zh: 我家二百年天子，顧不及崔、盧耶？」

translations.literal: Our house has been Son of Heaven for two hundred years—can we really not match the Cui and Lu clans?"
translations.idiomatic: Two centuries our house has ruled—are we truly beneath the Cuis and the Lus?"

sentences.zh: 詔宗正卿取世家子以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Director of the Imperial Clan to select sons of eminent houses and report.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Director of the Imperial Clan to nominate eligible sons of great families.

sentences.zh: 中立及校書郎衛洙得召見禁中，拜著作郎。

translations.literal: Zhongli and collation secretary Wei Zhu were summoned to audience within the palace and appointed as compilers in the Archive Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli and the collation secretary Wei Zhu were called into the inner palace and made compilers in the Archive Bureau.

sentences.zh: 月中，遷光祿少卿、駙馬都尉，尚真源長公主。

translations.literal: Within the month he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Grand Military Attendant, marrying the Princess of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Within the month he rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Grand Military Attendant, taking the Princess of Zhenyuan in marriage.

sentences.zh: 中立數求自試，憒憒不樂，因言：「朝廷法令備具，吾若不任事，何賴貴戚撓天下法耶？」

translations.literal: Zhongli repeatedly asked to prove himself, restless and discontent; he thus said: "The court's laws and orders are complete—if I do not take up duties, on what grounds should a noble relation bend the law of the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli pressed again and again for real responsibility, chafing at idleness; he declared: "The statutes of the realm stand complete—if I hold no actual post, what excuse has a kinsman of the throne to warp the law?"

sentences.zh: 帝聞異之，轉太仆、衛尉二少卿，歷左右金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor heard this with surprise and transferred him to the two vice directorships of the Court of the Imperial Stud and the Court of the Imperial Guard, then through the Left and Right Golden Guard commands.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, struck by his words, moved him through the vice directorships of the Stud and Guard courts and then the Left and Right commands of the Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 京師惡少優戲道中，具騶唱呵衛，自謂「盧言京兆」，驅放自如。

translations.literal: Ruffians in the capital put on farces in the streets, fully equipped with outriders and shouting guard escort, calling themselves "Lu, speaking for the metropolitan governor," driving and dispersing as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Street thugs in the capital staged mock processions with outriders and shouting heralds, styling one of their own "Lu, voice of the capital," and pushed pedestrians aside at will.

sentences.zh: 中立部從吏捕系，立箠死。

translations.literal: Zhongli's subordinate attendants seized and bound them, and immediately beat them to death with cudgels.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli's officers arrested them on the spot and clubbed them to death.

sentences.zh: 遷司農卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Court of the National Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Court of the National Granaries.

sentences.zh: 繩吏急，反為中傷，左徙慶王傅。

translations.literal: He tightened the leash on clerks severely and in turn was slandered, demoted to tutor of the Prince of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: His harsh discipline of the staff provoked counterattacks, and he was demoted to tutor of the Prince of Qing.

sentences.zh: 久之，復拜司農卿，入謝，帝曰：「卿用法深，信乎？」

translations.literal: After a long while he was again appointed Director of the Court of the National Granaries; entering to give thanks, the emperor said: "You apply the law with severity—is that so?"
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was reappointed Director of the National Granaries; at his audience of thanks the emperor asked, "They say you enforce the law harshly—is it true?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「轂下百司養名不肯事，如司農尤叢劇。

translations.literal: He answered: "Under the capital's hundred offices, many cultivate reputation and refuse work; the Granary Court above all is tangled and arduous.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "At the capital, countless offices hoard empty titles and shirk their work—the Granary Court is among the worst entanglements.

sentences.zh: 陛下無遽信流言，假臣數月，事可濟。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty, do not hastily believe slander; grant me a few months and the affair can be accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must not heed rumor too quickly—give me a few months and the work will be done."

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，度支度六宮飧錢移司農，司農季一出付吏，大吏盡舉所給於人，權其子錢以給之，既不以時，黃門來督責慢罵。

translations.literal: At first the Department of Revenue measured the palace meal funds and transferred them to the Granary Court; the Granary Court disbursed once per season to the clerks; senior clerks took all the allotments for themselves and advanced the interest money to pay out; since payment was not timely, eunuchs came to supervise and reproached them with insults.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the Revenue Department calculated the inner palace meal allowance and handed it to the Granary Court, which paid out once a quarter through its clerks—senior clerks skimmed the whole allotment and used the interest to make payments late, until eunuch overseers arrived to berate them.

sentences.zh: 中立取錢納帑舍，率五日一出，吏不得為奸，後遂以為法。

translations.literal: Zhongli took the funds into the treasury storeroom and paid out on average every five days; clerks could not commit fraud, and afterward this became standard practice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli had the cash deposited in the treasury vault and issued it every five days on a fixed schedule, cutting off clerical theft—and the system afterward became law.

sentences.zh: 加檢校右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Acting Right Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed Acting Right Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹缺，宣宗將用之，宰相以年少，欲歷試其能，更出為義武節度使。

translations.literal: The metropolitan governorship of Jingzhao was vacant; Emperor Xuanzong was about to appoint him, but the chief ministers, considering him young, wished to test his ability through experience, and instead sent him out as military governor of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital governorship fell open, Xuanzong meant to give it to him; the chief ministers thought him still young and preferred to test his mettle, so he was posted instead as military governor of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 舊傜車三千乘，歲免鹽海瀕，民苦之。

translations.literal: Formerly three thousand corvée carts annually shipped salt from the seacoast; the people suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Custom had bound the region to three thousand transport carts a year hauling salt from the coast, and the people groaned under the burden.

sentences.zh: 中立置「飛雪將」數百人，具舟以載，自是民不勞，軍食足矣。

translations.literal: Zhongli established several hundred "Flying Snow troops," fully equipped boats to carry the loads; from then on the people were not toiled and army provisions were sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: He organized several hundred "Flying Snow" carriers and shifted the cargo to boats—after that the people were spared, and the army's provisions were secure.

sentences.zh: 大中十二年，大水泛徐、兗、青、鄆，而滄地積卑，中立自按行，引禦水入之毛河，東註海，州無水災。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Dazhong, great floods spread through Xu, Yan, Qing, and Yun; Cangzhou's land lay low; Zhongli personally inspected and diverted the flood-control waters into the Mao River, flowing east into the sea, and the prefecture had no flood disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong 12 floods inundated Xu, Yan, Qing, and Yun; Cangzhou's lowlands were especially threatened—Zhongli toured the dikes himself, channeling the control waters into the Mao River and eastward to the sea, and the prefecture escaped disaster.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十八，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at age forty-eight; posthumously he was given Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-eight and was posthumously honored as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 中立居官精明，吏下寒栗畏伏。

translations.literal: Zhongli in office was sharp and clear; subordinate clerks shivered coldly in fear and submission.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli administered with razor-sharp precision; the staff beneath him trembled and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 中雖坐累免，及復用，亦不為寬假，其天資所長雲。

translations.literal: Though in between he was dismissed through accumulated charges, once reappointed he still would not relax leniency—such was the strength of his inborn nature.
translations.idiomatic: Even after demotion and reinstatement he never softened—strictness was simply his native bent.

sentences.zh: 杜亞，字次公，自雲本京兆人。

translations.literal: Du Ya, courtesy name Cigong, claimed his origin as a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ya, styled Cigong, traced his family to Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 肅宗在靈武，上書論當世事，擢校書郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong was at Lingwu, he submitted a memorial discussing current affairs and was promoted to collation secretary.
translations.idiomatic: While Suzong held court at Lingwu, he memorialized on affairs of the day and was raised to collation secretary.

sentences.zh: 杜鴻漸節度河西，奏署幕府。

translations.literal: When Du Hongjian was military governor of Hexi, he memorialized to appoint him to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hongjian, as military governor of Hexi, had him posted to his headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 入朝，歷吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered court and served successively as vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Called to the capital, he rose through posts as vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸為山南、劍南副元帥，亞與楊炎並為判官。

translations.literal: When Hongjian served as deputy commander-in-chief of Shannan and Jiannan, Ya and Yang Yan were both made adjutants.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongjian became deputy supreme commander for Shannan and Jiannan, Ya and Yang Yan served jointly as his adjutants.

sentences.zh: 再遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to Grand Censor of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: After two further promotions he held the post of Grand Censor of Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 亞自以當衡柄，悒悒不悅。

translations.literal: Ya considered himself fit for the scales of power and was sullen and displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Ya believed himself destined for the chancellorship and brooded in dissatisfaction.

sentences.zh: 李棲筠風望高，時謂當宰相，故亞厚結納。

translations.literal: Li Qiyun's reputation stood high; contemporaries said he would become chief minister, and therefore Ya cultivated a close bond with him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiyun commanded high esteem and was widely tipped for the chancellery—Ya drew him into a warm alliance.

sentences.zh: 元載得罪，亞與劉晏等劾治。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zai fell from grace, Ya joined Liu Yan and others in impeaching and prosecuting him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zai was brought down, Ya stood with Liu Yan and others to impeach and try him.

sentences.zh: 載死，遷給事中。

translations.literal: When Zai died, Ya was transferred to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After Zai's death he was promoted to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 常袞惡之，出為江西觀察使。

translations.literal: Chang Gun disliked him and sent him out as observation commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Gun, who despised him, had him posted as observation commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，召還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong acceded, he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong's accession brought his recall to court.

sentences.zh: 亞意必任臺宰，倍道進。

translations.literal: Ya was certain he would be appointed to the highest office of the secretariat and traveled at double speed.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced he would be named chief minister, Ya hastened toward the capital at breakneck pace.

sentences.zh: 與人語，皆天下大政。

translations.literal: In speaking with people, all his topics were great affairs of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Every conversation he held turned on the grand policies of the empire.

sentences.zh: 或以事祈謁，輒相然可。

translations.literal: When someone came to petition him on some matter, he would invariably agree.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever came to him with a request invariably won his ready assent.

sentences.zh: 帝知，不悅也。

translations.literal: The emperor learned of this and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of it, he was displeased.

sentences.zh: 既又建奏疏闊，不稱旨，罷為陜虢觀察兼轉運使。

translations.literal: Moreover his memorials were broad and loose and did not suit the emperor's intent; he was dismissed and made observation commissioner of Shan-Guo and concurrently transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials grew diffuse and missed the mark; he was removed and made observation commissioner of Shan-Guo with concurrent charge of transport.

sentences.zh: 徙河中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 劉晏抵罪，貶睦州刺史。

translations.literal: When Liu Yan was convicted, Ya was demoted to prefect of Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yan fell, Ya was demoted to prefect of Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 興元初，入遷刑部侍郎，又拜淮西節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan he entered court and was promoted to vice minister of justice, then appointed military governor of Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xingyuan era he returned to court as vice minister of justice, then was appointed military governor of Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 至則治漕渠，引湖陂，築防庸，入之渠中，以通大舟，夾堤高卬，田因得溉灌。

translations.literal: On arrival he repaired the transport canals, drew in lake embankments, built flood barriers, and channeled water into them so that large vessels could pass; the dikes on both sides were raised high, and fields thereby received irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he dredged the transport canals, tapped lake reservoirs, built floodworks, and fed them into the channels so large ships could pass; raised dikes on both banks brought irrigation to the fields.

sentences.zh: 疏啟道衢，徹壅通堙，人皆悅賴。

translations.literal: He cleared and opened the roads and thoroughfares, removed blockages and opened silted passages, and the people all rejoiced and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared the roads, removed obstructions, and opened blocked passages, to the people's great relief.

sentences.zh: 然承陳少遊後，裒率煩重，用度無藝，人冀有所矯革，而亞雅意丞弼，厭外官，往往不親事，日夜召賓客言噱流連。

translations.literal: Yet following Chen Shaoyou, levies were heavy and burdensome and expenditures unbounded; people hoped for some correction, but Ya secretly aspired to the chancellorship, disliked provincial office, often did not attend to affairs himself, and day and night summoned guests for jesting and lingering talk.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he inherited Chen Shaoyou's heavy levies and reckless spending; people hoped for reform, but Ya secretly coveted the chancellorship, disdained provincial office, neglected his duties, and spent day and night entertaining guests with banter and feasting.

sentences.zh: 方春，南民為競度戲，亞欲輕駛，乃髹船底，使篙人衣油彩衣，沒水不濡，觀沼華邃，費皆千萬。

translations.literal: In spring the southern people held dragon-boat races; Ya wished to race lightly, so he lacquered the boat bottoms and had the polemen wear oil-painted garments so that when submerged they were not soaked; the spectacle on the ponds was gorgeous and deep, and the costs ran to tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, when southerners held dragon-boat races, Ya wanted a swift spectacle: he lacquered the hulls and dressed the boatmen in oil-painted clothes that stayed dry underwater; the pageantry on the ponds was lavish, costing millions.

sentences.zh: 隴西李衡在坐，曰：「使桀、紂為之，不是過也！」

translations.literal: Li Heng of Longxi, seated there, said, "If Jie and Zhou had done this, it would not have exceeded it!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Heng of Longxi, who was present, remarked, "Jie and Zhou could hardly have outdone this!"

sentences.zh: 既泛九曲池，曳繡為帆，詫曰：「要當稱是林沼。」

translations.literal: Then they sailed on the Nine-Bend Pool, trailing brocade as sails, and he exclaimed, "This truly befits these woods and waters."
translations.idiomatic: They then sailed the Nine-Bend Pool with brocade rigged as sails, and he boasted, "Now this grove and pond are truly worthy of the name."

sentences.zh: 衡曰：「未有錦纜，云何？」

translations.literal: Heng said, "Without brocade mooring ropes, how so?"
translations.idiomatic: Heng asked, "Without brocade hawsers, how can you say that?"

sentences.zh: 亞大慚。

translations.literal: Ya was greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Ya was deeply embarrassed.

sentences.zh: 自是府財耗竭。

translations.literal: From then on the prefectural treasury was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the prefectural treasury was drained dry.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，罷歸。

translations.literal: During Zhenyuan he was dismissed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan era he was dismissed and returned home.

sentences.zh: 宰相竇參憚其宿望，以檢校吏部尚書留守東都。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Dou Can feared his long-standing reputation and made him acting Minister of the Civil Service with charge as regent of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Dou Can, wary of his standing, appointed him acting Minister of the Civil Service with charge as regent of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 病風痹且廢，猶欲固寵，奏墾苑中為營田，可減度支歲稟。

translations.literal: Sick with wind paralysis and nearly incapacitated, he still wished to secure favor and memorialized to reclaim land in the imperial park as garrison fields, which could reduce the annual grain allotment from the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Though crippled by paralysis, he still sought favor and memorialized to turn imperial parkland into garrison farms, claiming this would cut the annual grain subsidy from the Department of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 詔許之。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 先是，苑地可耕者，皆留司中人及屯士占假。

translations.literal: Earlier, all arable land in the park had been occupied on lease by palace staff and garrison soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, all cultivable parkland had been leased out to palace staff and garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 亞計窘，更舉軍帑錢與甸人，至秋取菽粟償息輸軍中，貧不能償者發囷窖略盡，流亡過半。

translations.literal: Ya's plan was strained; he further raised military treasury funds and lent them to local farmers, taking beans and grain with interest in autumn to deliver to the army; those too poor to repay had their granaries and cellars emptied, and more than half fled as refugees.
translations.idiomatic: Ya's scheme backfired: he lent military funds to local farmers at interest payable in grain each autumn; those who could not repay had their stores seized, and more than half the population fled.

sentences.zh: 又賂中人求兼河南尹。

translations.literal: He also bribed eunuchs to seek concurrent appointment as metropolitan governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He also bribed eunuchs to win concurrent appointment as metropolitan governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 帝審其妄，使禮部尚書董晉代之，賜亞還。

translations.literal: The emperor saw through his presumption, sent Minister of Rites Dong Jin to replace him, and granted Ya permission to return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw through his pretensions, sent Minister of Rites Dong Jin to replace him, and ordered Ya home.

sentences.zh: 病不能謁。

translations.literal: Ill, he could not attend audience.
translations.idiomatic: Too ill to attend court, he could not take leave.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十四，贈太子少傅，謚曰肅。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-four and was posthumously given Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent; his posthumous title was Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-four and was posthumously made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Solemn.

sentences.zh: 範傳正，字西老，鄧州順陽人。

translations.literal: Fan Chuanzheng, courtesy name Xilao, was a native of Shunyang in Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chuanzheng, style name Xilao, was from Shunyang in Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 父惀，為戶部員外郎，與趙郡李華善，有當世名。

translations.literal: His father Lun was a vice director in the Department of Revenue, was friendly with Li Hua of Zhao commandery, and had a name in his generation.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lun served as vice director in the Department of Revenue, was close to Li Hua of Zhao, and enjoyed renown in his day.

sentences.zh: 傳正舉進士、宏辭，皆高第，授集賢殿校書郎。

translations.literal: Chuanzheng passed the jinshi and hongci examinations, both with high ranks, and was appointed collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanzheng passed the jinshi and hongci examinations with top honors and was appointed collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 歷歙、湖、蘇三州刺史，有殊政，進拜宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of She, Hu, and Su, achieved outstanding administration, and was advanced to observation commissioner of Xuan-She.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of She, Hu, and Suzhou in turn, distinguished himself in office, and was promoted to observation commissioner of Xuan-She.

sentences.zh: 代還，坐治第過制，憲宗薄不用，改光祿卿。

translations.literal: When replaced and recalled, he was charged with building a residence exceeding regulations; Xianzong held him in low regard and did not employ him, and he was changed to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: On recall he was charged with building a residence that exceeded regulations; Xianzong looked on him coldly and reassigned him as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 以風痹卒，贈左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He died of wind paralysis and was posthumously given Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died of paralysis and was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 傳正好古，性精悍，初自整飭。

translations.literal: Chuanzheng loved antiquity, his nature was sharp and fierce, and at first he disciplined himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanzheng loved antiquity, was sharp and forceful by nature, and at first kept himself in strict order.

sentences.zh: 宦益達，用度益奢侈，傾貲貨市權貴歡，私公府如家帑，亦幸素有名，得不敗雲。

translations.literal: As his office rose ever higher, his expenditures grew ever more extravagant; he poured out wealth to purchase the favor of the powerful, treated the public treasury like his household funds, and also fortunately had long had a name, so he did not fall—so it is said.
translations.idiomatic: As he rose in office his spending grew lavish; he spent fortunes currying favor with the powerful and treated the public treasury as his own purse, yet his long-standing reputation spared him ruin—or so it is said.
